verdicts.floor_notes: L, effort 6, impact 7, risk 5, 10 files, est. 450-650 lines, 8 cases, gate architecture. Client-only: no Rust, bindings or IPC change, so it sits cleanly inside DECISIONS section 40.6. Not a re-proposal (backlog and STATUS hold nothing on validate mirrors; STATUS:1493 deleted a different mirror, owner/preview.ts).
verdicts.overlap: Duplicates wallet-domain-primitives slot A (same drift, same files: mandateDraft.ts(+test), mock/simulate.ts(+test)). This is the stronger formulation: it collapses the two TS logic copies into one, makes the mock sign path refuse like Rust, and fixes the scale fixture plus the test that certifies it, all without touching Rust. Build this one and void the other. It also has a semantic dependency with owner-mandate-config slot B, which uses ruleProblems as its oracle and asserts on its wording: build A first, or keep ruleProblems' output stable (see revision).
verdicts.ambition_why: It removes a drift class, backed by a live bug the scout found (the mock signs and certifies a rule the wallet refuses), with a parity test that turns a Rust change red on the client.
verdicts.grounding_why: Every cited fact holds, but the body's plan to turn M6 into a 'nine-clause rescue rule' is wrong for the tree: about 45% of scale shop_order deals are signed under M6 (scale.ts:568), and a rescue mandate cannot act on them.
verdicts.falsifiability_why: Cases 2-6 are red today and pin exact Rust reasons; case 7 must compare clause-number sets, not ordered lists; case 8 is mostly green today and works as a guard.
verdicts.revision: Add an acceptance case: for the 6 golden drafts of case 7, ruleProblems(previewClauses(d)) deep-equals its output at b563874. That keeps the editor's per-condition wording, such as 'it ends after the rules themselves end' and the 'X is required' lines, instead of collapsing into Rust's coarse reasons ('invalid band', 'required clause missing'). This forces validateRules to carry a per-condition detail under each Rust reason, and it protects slot B's oracle.
verdicts.builder_notes: (1) Fix M6 by dropping its lever clause (it stays a shop rule with the other 8 kinds and keeps its shop_order deals). Do NOT reshape it into a rescue rule. (2) Rust's validate() is first-error-only; validateRules may continue past it, but validateRules(p)[0] must equal Rust's first refusal exactly, including the currency check iterating clauses in given (unsorted) order and returning the clause number where the mismatch is found. (3) The parity test reads mandate.rs source text (precedent: notices.test.ts, contrast.test.ts read files). Slice by fn name, not line numbers. Refusal::new takes impl Into<String>. (4) Once mock mandate_sign validates, re-run lib/clientRequests.test.ts:145 and mock/firstRun.test.ts:90 (both sign through the mock) and the director/judge flows. (5) The card says '~23' reasons; there are 24 (REFUSAL_WORDS has 24 keys). (6) marketWatch.ts marketWatchRefusal is another partial copy of clause 9; fold it in or keep it as the clause-9 arm.

verdicts.floor_notes: M, effort 6, impact 8, risk 5, 12 files (2 generated), est. 500-700 lines, 7 cases, gate contract (in-repo bindings only). It changes Rust (table-core validate) and bindings, which DECISIONS section 40.6 ('No Rust ... bindings change') forbids for the console rebuild. Main has taken Rust and bindings commits since (0ff522b), so it is not a hard void on that alone, but it is a cost slot A does not pay.
verdicts.overlap: Same target as owner-mandate-config slot A (mandateDraft.ts(+test), mock/simulate.ts(+test)). It also shares table-client lib.rs, generate-bindings.rs and tests/bindings.rs with wallet-domain-primitives slot B.
verdicts.ambition_why: Typed problem codes in Rust are the principled end state, but the card stops halfway: mockValidate and ruleProblems remain two hand-written TS logic copies (the mock only 'gains' the lever checks), so the logic drift it names stays open.
verdicts.grounding_why: Premises hold. It cites 23 reasons; there are 24.
verdicts.falsifiability_why: Case 1 is not satisfiable as written. Empty roles plus a per_deal clause also yields the clause-1 'no role can act' problem (acting is empty), and without a per_deal clause it yields RequiredClauseMissing{3}, so problems() can never equal exactly those three.
verdicts.void_reason: Superseded by owner-mandate-config slot A, which targets the same duplication and closes more of it: one TS logic copy instead of two, mock mandate_sign validation, and the scale M6 fixture plus its dishonest test, with no Rust or bindings change under the section 40.6 freeze. This card leaves both TS logic copies in place, edits money-path validate() in table-core, and its first acceptance case is unsatisfiable. Keep the typed-codes idea as a later follow-up once the freeze lifts.
verdicts.builder_notes: Not to be built. If revived: problems() must suppress dependent checks (e.g. role-acts when roles is empty), or case 1 changes; validate() == problems().first() must reproduce the in-clause early-return order exactly; f1_refusal_message_is_exact and RefusalCode::from_refusal (agent.rs:509, which reads the typed cause) must stay green.

verdicts.floor_notes: M, effort 5, impact 7, risk 4, 12 files, est. 300-450 lines, 6 cases, gate none. It adds a Rust fn and a generated bindings file (no command, event or authority change). That touches section 40.6's 'no Rust/bindings' rule in the same way as above; flag it to the coordinator. Not a re-proposal: 0b7c534 (p-fc5755) unified the Rust-side predicates across core and ledger, and this card extends that to the client copies and graph derivation. Declare it as building on p-fc5755.
verdicts.overlap: Shares crates/table-client/src/lib.rs, src/bin/generate-bindings.rs and tests/bindings.rs (the produced list) with wallet-domain-primitives slot A. If both were built they would need serializing; moot if slot A is voided.
verdicts.ambition_why: A sound single-source move (graph-derived predicates, generated client sets) that fixes two real mock drifts, but it is a consolidation, not a principal-level shift.
verdicts.grounding_why: Rust and client facts hold, and the BFS arithmetic checks out (through-AGREED = 14 states; minus released = the 11 in is_agreed_or_later). Rust's fair-price 'committed' is history-based, though: market.rs:236-285 marks it true once an agreement row exists, so VOIDED, AUTO_VOIDED and EXPIRED are committed.
verdicts.falsifiability_why: Case 6 expects fairPriceOf('EXPIRED').committed true, but none of the five generated sets yields that. Swapping fairPrice to agreed_or_later makes EXPIRED false and regresses VOIDED/AUTO_VOIDED to false, so the case cannot pass under the card's own design.
verdicts.revision: Add a sixth generated set, through_agreed (the BFS set from case 2: states reachable only through AGREED, including VOIDED, AUTO_VOIDED and EXPIRED), and make fairPrice.ts use it instead of agreed_or_later. Extend case 6 to also assert fairPriceOf('VOIDED').committed -> true and fairPriceOf('MISMATCH').committed -> false.
verdicts.builder_notes: bindings/dealStates.ts is generated: run generate-bindings, and add it to the produced list in tests/bindings.rs:39 plus a freshness assert (the orphan gate fails otherwise). forecast.ts must keep CAPTURED/RECEIPTED as named 'nothing left to schedule' extras on top of Rust terminal(), or mock forecast lines change.
